title: Nanomanipulation of Single RNA Molecules by Optical Tweezers
protocol: Clone the sequence of interest into a vector.
Synthesize a transcription template by PCR.
Purify the PCR products using a PCR purification kit.
Concentrate the purified DNA sample to >200 ng/µl.
Synthesize RNA by in vitro transcription at 37 °C overnight.
Add 1 µl DNase I and incubate for 15 min at 37 °C to digest the DNA template.
Purify the RNA using a silica spin column.
Produce unmodified handle A by PCR using primers Af and Ar.
Concentrate the amplified DNA of unmodified handle A to >200 ng/µl.
Incorporate biotin modifications into the PCR product using primer extension reaction.
Synthesize digoxigenin modified handle B (dig-HB) by PCR using primer Bf and Dig-Br.
Purify the PCR product of digoxigenin-modified handle B.
Concentrate the purified sample to >200 ng/µl.
Anneal RNA with handles.
Add 3 volumes of ethanol to the annealed sample and mix well.
Store the mixture at -70°C for at least 1 hour.
Spin down the mixture at 15,800 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Dry the pellet using a lyophilizer.
Dissolve the pellet in 100 μl RNase-free water.
Store the sample at -20°C.
Use the optical trap to trap a bead with known diameter (size standard).
Capture images of a trapped bead using imaging software.
Determine the diameter of the bead using the centroid method.
Repeat this procedure for beads of different sizes.
Fit the measured and known diameters of the beads by linear regression to obtain the physical size of a pixel.
Use the optical trap to trap a bead.
Determine the pixel position of its centroid by image capture software.
Record the position using Minitweezers.
Steer the bead to different positions.
Repeat the position determination for each new position.
Convert the X and Y positions from pixels to meters using the calibrated pixel size.
Compare the X and Y positions measured by video and by the Minitweezers.
Move the bead over 1 µm between measurements for accuracy.
Recalibrate the instrument if distance calibration differs from stored values.
Capture a bead using the optical trap and hold it still.
Record the force of the trap at a rate >5 kHz for 3 seconds.
Generate a power spectrum from the recording of the bead motion.
Fit the power spectrum to a Lorentzian function.
Compute the spring constant of the trap from fc.
Use the spring constant to determine extension changes of an RNA from force change.
Capture a bead using the optical trap.
Move the bead back-and-forth at different speeds.
Record the motion and force of the bead using the Minitweezers.
Compute the radius of the bead using Stokes’ law.
Drill six holes (2 mm diameter each) on a No. 2 cover glass.
Cut three slits (2 mm width) into double-sided polyimide tape using a laser engraver.
Sandwich two cover glass with two layers of double-sided Kapton tape to make a flow chamber.
Insert a micropipette and two bypass tubes between the tape in the flow chamber.
Mount the flow chamber onto a metal frame by matching fluidic holes.
Connect the fluidic channels of the chamber to 10 ml syringes filled with buffer via polyethylene tubings.
Mount the entire chamber onto the optical tweezers between the two objectives.
Ensure that the front side of the chamber with the fluidic channels faces to the right.
Retract the right objective and plug the brass pins of the frame into mounting holes on the tweezers.
Tighten screws to fix the chamber position.
Mix the annealed sample with anti-digoxigenin-coated beads (dig-beads).
Let the mixture stay at room temperature for 5-10 min.
Load a suspension of streptavidin-coated beads (strep-beads) into a 1 ml syringe.
Connect the syringe to the fluidic tubing leading to the bottom channel of the flow chamber.
Push the syringe to flow the strep-beads into the chamber.
Move the chamber using motor control software to position the optical trap near the bottom bypass tube opening.
Operate the optical trap with a trackball to capture a strep-bead.
Use the motor control software to move the bead close to the micropipette tip.
Pull the syringe connected to the micropipette to suction the bead onto it.
Apply gentle flow by pressing the syringe to flush out extra strep-beads from the channel.
Deliver the mixture of sample and dig-beads to the top channel using the motor control software.
Capture a dig-bead with the optical trap.
Move the captured dig-bead close to the previously attached strep-bead.
Clean the middle channel by applying flow gently.
Place the dig-bead vertically on top of the strep-bead.
Steer the trap to move the dig-bead down towards the strep-bead.
Open a force-distance plot window on the computer to monitor force changes.
Upon contact of the two beads, move the dig-bead vertically away from the strep-bead.
